title: Vignette: we don't keep something that is wrong; the spec does what is expected

sections.name: words
sections.content:
Let's think about this principle.

We also don't want to keep something that is wrong.

Where possible we want the srs spec do what is expected... When we pick a counter intuitive option over over that is obviously easier to understand and has no obvious downside, then we should do what is better

sections.name: context
sections.content: Said 2026-11-27 in reply to the option set for srs#1035 (RFC-051 Rev 16 tie-break). The recommendation had been to codify srs-rust's existing tie rule (compare tied runs from the last entry backwards, keep the lower key) on Reliability over Renewal, because it changes no tool or data, over a more intuitive rule (e.g. keep the earliest run in the new outline).
